observation_summary: The iterator() method in ListPopulation returned the iterator of the internal modifiable list directly, allowing external code to modify the population's internal state (e.g., removing chromosomes) which violated the expected encapsulation.
hypothesis: The iterator() method was incorrectly implemented by exposing the internal list's iterator directly, rather than using a safe, unmodifiable view of the list.
prediction: The fix will change the implementation of iterator() to return an iterator from a method that provides an unmodifiable view of the chromosomes, such as getChromosomes().
experiment_rationale: The fix diff shows that the implementation was changed from returning 'chromosomes.iterator()' to 'getChromosomes().iterator()'. This confirms that the original method logic was flawed because it failed to respect the encapsulation of the internal data structure.
reasoning_summary: The bug is an incorrect implementation of the iterator() method. It is not a missing check (Checking), nor a wrong value (Assignment/Initialization), nor a design-level capability omission (Function/Class/Object). It is a procedural error in how the iterator is provided, which is best classified as an Algorithm/Method defect as it involves correcting the internal logic of the method to ensure proper data encapsulation.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: While this involves an interface (Iterator), the root cause is the internal implementation logic of the ListPopulation class, not a mismatch in the contract between two components.
The capability (iterator) existed, but its implementation was flawed. It does not require a design-level change to the class structure.
